pictures.c: Block-diagram of the Ufita River Valley. The gently-dipping faceted spurs are interpreted as evidence for a normal fault, while the surface to the right is interpreted as a glacis (from Brancaccio et al. [1981], modified).

pictures.t: Fault model by Pantosti and Valensise [1989]
pictures.c: Area of largest damage for the 1732 earthquake (from Pantosti and Valensise [1989]).
The source of the 1857 earthquake was first described as a large, NE-dipping normal fault within the segmentation model referred to as "Faglia Sud-Appenninica" (from Pantosti and Valensise [1988]).

pictures.t: Geologic and tectonic map [Basso et al., 1996b]
pictures.c: Geological map of the Ufita River Valley, showing an inferred normal fault on its NE flank, and the overflooding of the basin over an 8 km-long stretch between Castel Baronia and Grottaminarda (from Basso et al. [1996b]).
Geomorphological map of the Ufita River Valley. Notice that symbol 6 and 7/8 indicate fluvio-lacustrine deposits and erosional surfaces, respectively (from Basso et al. [1996a]).

pictures.t: Cross section of Ufita River valley [Basso et al., 1996a]
pictures.c: Cross-section across the Ufita River valley derived from correlation of well stratigraphies (from Basso et al. [1996a]).
